chunks: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not leave the people with any authority in their religion except for them [the Imams] or for those whom they appointed to it from the Ahl al-Bayt or those whom they authorized in it.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt (the Family of the Prophet, specifically the Imams)

ai.seo_question: Who holds the authority to interpret and govern religious law according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to articulate the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (explicit designation), emphasizing that divine authority is not merely theoretical but requires specific, appointed leadership to preserve religious integrity. This establishes the Imams as the infallible interpreters of the Quran and the sole legitimate sources of religious law after the Prophet, ensuring the continuity of divine guidance through a clear chain of authority.
